extracted.intended_audience: science fiction & fantasy short fiction authors, editors, and awards-interested readers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative criteria for Hugo and Nebula awards for short fiction, including length categories, eligibility timing, award voting bodies, nomination/voting procedures, and genre-specific quality criteria for SF/F short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Story (length)
rubrics_metrics.description: < 7,500 words

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel (length)
rubrics_metrics.description: 40,000+ words

rubrics_metrics.name: Hugo Award: voter base & evaluative stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Voted by WorldCon supporting/attending members; 'Barometer of reader popularity rather than artistic merit'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No formal criteria — reflects what genre readers loved most.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nebula Award: voter base
rubrics_metrics.description: Voted by SFWA active members (published professional SF/F writers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is by professional peers rather than general reader voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nebula Award: evaluative stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides 'more literary judgment'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied emphasis on craft and literary qualities as assessed by professional writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nebula nomination restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors cannot nominate own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nebula ballot formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Top 6 nominations form ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nebula final voting process
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners chosen by month-long member vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of wonder
rubrics_metrics.description: Sense of wonder — the genre's central affect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The emotional or imaginative awe associated with speculative fiction; a core genre expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual originality — a fresh idea, twist, or world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality can be in premise, twist, or world-construction; rewards novel concepts or unexpected treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldbuilding economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Worldbuilding economy — establishes setting in few strokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efficiently conveys setting/rules without long exposition; implies clarity and selective detail appropriate to short forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal consistency — invented rules followed rigorously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculative elements should behave according to their own established logic; avoids deus ex machina or rule-breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-anchored
rubrics_metrics.description: Character-anchored — speculative concept made personal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong short fiction often grounds big ideas in a character's experience or perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonant ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Resonant ending — emotional or intellectual snap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endings should provide an emotional or cognitive payoff; memorable closure or twist that resonates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with the genre tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement with the genre tradition — knows what came before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should show awareness of SF/F conventions and history; can build on, subvert, or converse with tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social/political commentary via speculative metaphor
rubrics_metrics.description: Often: social/political commentary through speculative metaphor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculative elements frequently serve as metaphor for contemporary issues; this is a common and valued approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: first English publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: First English publication in a calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is tied to the year of first English-language publication; timing matters for which year's ballot a work is eligible for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: genre scope
rubrics_metrics.description: All science fiction, fantasy, or related fiction genres eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awards accept works across SF/F and related speculative genres; cross-genre works are included if within SF/F scope.
